subject: Chinchilla native sprite

requests.prompt:
Create a NEW standalone pixel-art DESIGN REFERENCE storyboard, not an edit of the previous factory pictures. Subject: a tiny CHINCHILLA rodent enemy for a side-view pixel platformer in a green GPU furnace. Cute but unnervingly compact and heavy, an extremely small tanky animal rather than an armored robot.
Use exactly THREE equal panels in ONE horizontal row, same scale, same side-on three-quarter LEFT-facing view, same ground contact line. The creature is only about16 native pixels tall and18 pixels wide including its tail, centered inside a32x32 sprite. Show intentionally large pixel clusters at an integer enlargement so this tiny design remains readable; do NOT add resolution, fine hair or portrait detail.
Distinctive anatomy: two large ROUND short ears, broad grey cheeks, a BLUNT short muzzle, tiny dark eye, compact pear-shaped hindquarters, short front paws and a large tucked hind foot. A thick FURRY tail curves low behind the rump, with a small upturned tip. Keep the tail separate from the hind foot. Not rabbit ears, not a long pointed rat nose, not a bare rat tail, not a towering squirrel tail. No clothes, armor, weapons, text or machinery.
Panel1 idle: alert squat, round ears upright, paws planted. Panel2 tell: subtle bracing, ears angle outward, tiny forepaws tighten; main body and ground anchor stay stable. Panel3 recover: release after a dense burst, cheeks or front paws relax and the tail tip settles1 pixel. This is a three-state pose reference, NOT a walk cycle; no jump and no new attack effect.
Upper-left light, hard pixel edges, selective dark outline, compact broad fur highlights. Palette roles: outline/nose2c2330; cool fur shadows34354f, mid575c79, highlight858eb0; small warm muzzle/bellycbb696/f5e8c8; subdued plum inner ears723f68. No orange, no glow, no gradients, no anti-aliasing, no checker texture. Limit the design to seven opaque colors. Plain neutral dark background, no ground shadow, scenery, labels, separators, border or watermark. This reference will be redrawn natively; preserve the tiny silhouette rather than embellishing it.
